02Upstairs bedroom

One room, rewired without tearing out the plaster.

  1. 01

    Open two small cuts

    One at the top of the wall, one behind the outlet. Not a trench across the room.

  2. 02

    Fish the new wire

    New cable drops through the wall cavity from the attic, beside the old knob-and-tube, which is cut off and retired.

  3. 03

    Test it and label it

    The outlet is tested and the circuit is written into a labeled panel, so you know which breaker runs which room.

  4. 04

    Patch, then the next room

    The cuts are patched before we leave. Tomorrow we start the next room while you live in the rest.

05Living room

Two-hole outlets have three honest fixes.

A three-prong outlet on a circuit with no ground only looks safer. Here is what each fix does, and when it fits.

Run a ground wire

A ground is pulled from the panel to the outlet, and a true three-prong outlet goes in. The most complete fix, and a good fit when walls are already open for a rewire.

Fits when: you plug in computers, a fridge or anything with a three-prong cord.

GFCI protection

A GFCI outlet cuts the power in a fraction of a second if current leaks, even with no ground wire. It carries a "No equipment ground" label so the next owner knows.

Fits when: the walls are closed and you want shock protection without opening plaster.

Replace like for like

If the wiring behind it is sound, a worn two-hole outlet is swapped for a new two-hole one. No false promise of a ground that is not there.

Fits when: the outlet only feeds lamps and two-prong cords.

Two-prong outlet update: $180–$400 per outlet · grounded or GFCI-protected Sample pricing

06Detached garage

Plan the run from the panel to the car.

Most bungalow garages sit at the back of the lot. The distance, and whether the wire goes overhead or in a trench, moves the price more than the charger does.

Garage on the houseBack of the houseDetached, across the yard
  • Short run on the same wall: the low end of the range is realistic.
  • Run through the basement or along the eaves: middle of the range.
  • Trench or overhead line to a detached garage: the high end, and we plan the route around trees with you.

EV charger installation: $850 to $2,400 (longer runs to a detached garage cost more) Sample pricing
